newsitem.title: USA: Deere says sees strong demand, '97 volume.
newsitem.headline: Deere says sees strong demand, '97 volume.

text.p: Deere & Co said Tuesday it sees strong demand for its agricultural and construction equipment in 1997, and that its planned comparable physical sales volume is expected to increase by 11 percent over 1996, a larger gain than previously expected.

It also said it increased its fourth-quarter 1997 comparable physical volume of sales, which is expected to be eight percent above the year-ago period, said Hans Becherer, Deere & Co chairman and chief executive officer, in an earnings release.

"The company's excellent financial results and the continued strong demand for our products provide a solid base for future operations," Becherer said. "Based on these factors, we expect continued excellent operations performance."
He also said negotiations are underway with the United Auto Workers (UAW) on a new labor agreement to replace the current agreement that expires Oct 1, 1997.
"It is premature to determine the results of these discussions," Becherer said.
Deere & Co reported third-quarter earnings of $1.00 per share versus $0.79 in the year-ago period. It said third-quarter sales and revenues rose 18 percent to $3.43 billion from $2.90 billion.
